title: 20 Things I Learned - Canvas Book Page Flip

affordance_translation.physical_behavior: A hardcover book: grab the page edge, the sheet bends and curls over the spine with a folding shadow, and settles on the other side.
affordance_translation.digital_mechanic: Google's HTML5 case study (web.dev): each page is a section with a flip object tracking progress/target/dragging; dragging near the spine bends the page via canvas rendering - fold position, page bend strength and progressive left/right shadows are all derived from flip progress. Release completes the flip or snaps back depending on drag side.

design_tokens.borders: Book cover with rounded spine; page edges shaded by fold geometry, no UI borders
design_tokens.elevation: Dynamic fold shadow computed per frame (left/right shadow width from bend strength) - depth is the flip itself
design_tokens.typography: Storybook serif with large initials, warm paper background texture

interactive_mechanics: Drag a page edge to bend and flip; release physics decides complete vs snap-back
zIndex stacking per page with continuous flip progress
Canvas-drawn curl: page masked at foldX with animated fold shadow
Arrow-key page turns as the keyboard equivalent
usability_notes: The canonical reference implementation (web.dev full source walkthrough). Page flip earns its cost only for linear, chapter-like content (guides, annual reports, lookbooks); for arbitrary navigation it impedes scanning - always pair with a persistent index or progress bar, keep flip animation under ~500ms, and support swipe plus arrows. Text must stay selectable/accessible outside the canvas-rendered fold frames.
